question:
Approve this outcome and scope to advance to spec?

This feature writes into live production data that two people use daily, which no prior feature in this workflow has done. Three things are worth your call now rather than at spec:

(1) Reversibility as a hard requirement. The seed makes "a stated, exercised way to undo the migration" a success condition, and staging-first a spec question. Confirm that stands: no import runs until undo has been demonstrated, not just described.

(2) Does 2023 data actually exist? 060's recorded spec finding says the archive holds no 2023 record at all. You have pointed at tab gid=0 and asked to migrate "2024, 2023". Spec settles this by looking. If 2023 has no record, this feature covers 2024 only.

(3) The taxonomy does not fit. Your records carry 25 top-level buckets over 61 sub-categories with four row-kind tags; the app uses a flat gov_category set. Either the app's category set grows to fit history, or the import approximates and some detail is lost on the way in. That is your decision, not an implementer's. Spec will put the options in front of you — confirm you want it raised there rather than settled now.

artifacts.summary:
Outcome: the app itself holds the captain's 2023 and 2024 expense records, so those years are visible alongside day-to-day logging instead of living only in Google Sheets. Feasibility is judged and reported before any write is attempted.

Scope: 2023 and 2024 only. A written feasibility verdict first (possible, possible-with-caveats, or not possible, with the reason). If feasible, those records land in the app with correct categories, dates, and amounts; existing data is proven intact by a before/after check rather than asserted; and an exercised undo path exists.

Excluded: all other archive years (060 inventories and analyses those); the growth analysis itself; any new app UI for browsing historical years; and any change to how the app treats categories going forward beyond what landing these two years requires.

Proof spec owes: whether 2023 data exists, settled by inspecting tab gid=0 rather than assuming; a decision surface for the 25-bucket to flat-gov_category mismatch; a ruling on rental-property pass-through and income rows, which distort every app total if imported silently; the aggregate-row filter, since section totals sit interleaved with real line items and importing them double-counts; the per-year source-file pick rule where duplicate, template, and legacy .xls variants exist; and the undo plus blast-radius plan, including whether the run happens against staging first.

Dependency: this feature blocks 060-historical-expense-analysis. The captain chose migration-first, so the 2006-2025 growth report is specced after this lands and may read the migrated data as a source.
